title: Stuffed Pepper Soup
tagline: Every part of a stuffed pepper, none of the stuffing.
description: Ground beef, bell peppers, tomatoes and rice in one pot: all of the stuffed-pepper flavor in about an hour, with none of the hollowing, stuffing or baking. Rice is cooked on the side so leftovers stay soup, not porridge.
ingredients: 3 bell peppers (any mix of green, red, yellow), diced, about 3 cups
1 1/2 tsp Diamond Crystal kosher salt (3/4 tsp table salt), divided, plus more to taste
1 can (14.5 oz / 411g) diced tomatoes, with juice
1 cup (100g) shredded cheddar or mozzarella, for topping
steps: Heat oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high. Add beef and break it up; cook 6-8 minutes, without stirring constantly, until no pink remains and the bottom of the pot has browned bits. Spoon off all but about 1 Tbsp of fat.
Add onion, peppers and 1 tsp of the salt. Cook 6-8 minutes, stirring now and then, until the onion is soft and the peppers have lost their raw crunch.
Add garlic, tomato paste, oregano, paprika and pepper. Stir 1 minute until the paste darkens to brick red.

Pour in diced tomatoes, tomato sauce, broth, Worcestershire and brown sugar. Scrape the bottom of the pot clean. Bring to a boil, then lower to a gentle simmer, partly covered, 20 minutes until the peppers are fully tender.

While the soup simmers, cook the rice: bring rice, 1 1/2 cups water and the remaining 1/2 tsp salt to a boil in a small saucepan, cover, drop to low and cook 18 minutes. Off heat, leave covered 5 minutes, then fluff.
Taste the soup and adjust salt. A splash of broth thins it if it got too thick.
Spoon rice into bowls, ladle soup over, top with cheese and parsley.
notes: Rice stays separate on purpose. Cooked in the pot, it keeps drinking broth in the fridge and day-two soup turns into a casserole.
Want it all in one pot anyway: stir the raw rice in at the start of the 20-minute simmer with 1 extra cup of broth, and simmer until the rice is tender. Eat it the same day.
Freezes well without the rice, up to 3 months. Cook fresh rice when you reheat.
Green peppers taste most like the classic stuffed pepper; red and yellow make it sweeter.
troubleshooting: Tastes flat → under-salted or under-browned beef; salt to taste and let the beef really brown before the vegetables go in.
Too sharp or acidic → tomatoes vary; add brown sugar 1/2 tsp at a time.
Greasy surface → fat not drained after browning; skim with a wide spoon or lay a paper towel on the surface for a second.
Thick and stodgy leftovers → rice was stored in the soup; thin with broth when reheating, and store rice separately next time.
